summary: Ephemeral scaler heartbeat drift causing elevated 5xx and long-tail latency in us-east production
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat Labs (dedicated) reported a sudden increase in 5xx responses and long-tail tail latency on streaming and short-sync generation routes starting during the 09:15-09:45 UTC window in us-east. Impact: several production endpoints returning 502/503 and occasional 504, increased first-byte times up to 8s for affected requests.

Impact:
- BrightChat experienced degraded UX across chat and batch embeddings; multiple customer sessions timed out and retried.
- Platform-level metrics show API gateway threadpool saturation and a correlated spike in upstream runtime connection churn.

Environment:
- prod | us-east; affected routes: /v1/chat/stream and /v1/embeddings/bulk.
- Customer on dedicated capacity pool: shard dc-dedicated-45.

Steps to reproduce (observed pattern):
1) Send burst of mixed streaming and embedding requests (small payloads, high concurrency) to BrightChat tenant.
2) After ~20s, several ephemeral runtimes start failing health checks and drop connections.
3) API gateway threads queue up and return 502/503 when backpressure exceeds threadpool limits.

Observed behavior:
- Heartbeat misses from ephemeral scheduler to proxy; runtimes flagged unhealthy and removed from routing.
- Rapid reconnect attempts from many clients cause socket churn and keepalive exhaustion.

Expected behavior:
- Ephemeral scaler should maintain stable heartbeat windows during scale-up and not trigger mass eviction. Runtimes should warm gracefully without overloading the API gateway.
steps_to_reproduce: Issue observed during mixed streaming+embedding burst against BrightChat tenant in us-east
Synthetic reproduction: 200 concurrent short streaming sessions + 10 parallel bulk-embed uploads over 30s
Monitor api-gateway threadpool, ephemeral scheduler heartbeats, and runtime health events during the burst

comments: Support (Aisha): Customer noticed an uptick in 5xx starting ~09:15 UTC; they captured SDK logs and retry traces. Asked for immediate triage and suggested temporary rate limiting.

SRE (Tomás Rivera) 2026-03-12 10:03: Observed synchronized heartbeat misses from the ephemeral scheduler across >60% of pool nodes for dc-dedicated-45. Correlated with a config sweep to scheduler.timeout_ms that landed at 09:12 UTC.

Eng (Elena Brooks) 2026-03-12 11:10: Confirmed heartbeat window drift after config sweep — value decreased from 12000ms -> 4000ms in the control plane; some warmup tasks exceed new window leading to false negatives and eviction.

SRE (Tomás) 2026-03-12 11:35: Applied mitigation: rolled back scheduler.timeout_ms to 12000ms for dc-dedicated-45; manually re-added evicted runtimes to routing; observed error rate drop within 7 minutes.
Customer (BrightChat CSM) 2026-03-12 12:05: Customer verified restored traffic and reported improved response behavior; will keep monitoring for regressions.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 09:12 UTC: control-plane config sweep pushed a new scheduler heartbeat timeout (4000ms) to several dedicated pools as part of a normal rollout.
- 09:15 UTC onward: workloads with mixed streaming and embedding caused ephemeral runtimes to exceed the tighter heartbeat window during scale-up/warmup.
- False unhealthy markings produced mass evictions; clients retried, driving socket churn and apigw threadpool exhaustion.
- Metrics: apigw threadpool utilization peaked at 98%; runtime connection churn increased by 8x; evicted count peaked at 52 instances for dc-dedicated-45.
- Root cause: too-aggressive heartbeat timeout combined with prewarm tasks that block the scheduler event loop briefly (IO-bound checkpointing on some runtimes).
- Secondary contributing factors: default keepalive pool size for apigw was near threshold for this tenant's historical burst pattern, leaving little headroom during reconnection waves.
resolution_notes:
Short-term mitigations completed:
1) Rolled back scheduler.timeout_ms to 12000ms for affected dedicated pools (dc-dedicated-45).
2) Manually reintroduced healthy runtimes and triggered a staggered prewarm to avoid sync eviction.
3) Applied temporary tenant-level client QPS throttle for BrightChat (set to 75% of baseline) until rollout fully validated.
4) Increased apigw keepalive pool soft limit by 20% for us-east edge to absorb reconnect spikes.

Longer-term actions (tracked as follow-ups):
- Engineering will harden rollout gating for scheduler control-plane changes (PR linked) to include canary traffic patterns and an automated rollback if unhealthy evictions exceed threshold.
- Adjust default prewarm behavior to reduce blocking IO on warmup paths; add non-blocking checkpoint stream.
- Add an alert rule: sudden cluster-wide heartbeat miss rate >5% triggers immediate rollback and alert.
- Ownership: Autoscaler team to deliver patch in runtime repo and a scheduled canary to validate in staging with synthetic mixed workload.

Workaround for customers: use per-tenant rate limiting or stagger client-side reconnection with exponential backoff.
